items.author: Cointelegraph by Sam Bourgi
items.content:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, Trezor is reducing its authorized reseller network after reports of tampered Ledger wallets, MediaMarktSaturn pulled Ledger products from stores and online platforms and Aptos launched an encrypted transaction feature to protect traders from frontrunning and sandwich attacks.
Trezor cuts reseller network after Ledger wallet tampering reports
Hardware wallet maker Trezor is reducing its authorized reseller network after reports that a Southeast Asian reseller modified Ledger devices to steal users’ recovery phrases.
Trezor said Tuesday the decision was precautionary and that it had no evidence its own devices were compromised. Chief commercial officer Danny Sanders said affected resellers would lose their authorized status on Jan. 1, with shipments to those businesses stopping immediately.
The move follows rival Ledger’s confirmation that at least one device sold by reseller CryptoBilis contained an unauthorized hardware implant capable of capturing recovery phrases and transmitting them over cellular networks.
The incident has raised questions about the security of hardware wallet supply chains. Trezor told Cointelegraph that its existing checks can detect counterfeit devices and modified firmware, but the Ledger implant operated differently by reading information displayed on the device’s screen.
Blockchain investigators have estimated potential losses of between $72 million and $86 million, although Ledger said it had not confirmed the total.
Trezor advised customers to purchase devices directly from the manufacturer and consider multisignature wallets using hardware from different providers.
MediaMarktSaturn pulls Ledger products amid tampering reports
MediaMarktSaturn, the parent company of European electronics retailer MediaMarkt, has removed Ledger products from its physical stores and online platforms amid reports of tampered hardware wallets.
“The products have been removed from our product lineup internationally in all of our countries. We did this as a precautionary measure,” a MediaMarktSaturn spokesperson told Cointelegraph.
Ledger said Tuesday that MediaMarktSaturn suspended sales in coordination with the wallet maker following a report of a hardware implant from a customer in Germany. Ledger said no fund losses had been reported in connection with that case and that it had no indication its infrastructure, systems or services were compromised.
An X user known as Johannes claimed Monday that he purchased two Ledger wallets from separate MediaMarkt stores. He said both contained unauthorized cables and cellular modules.
The security concerns emerged Friday after Ledger said it is investigating reports of losses involving devices sold through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis. Ledger said Tuesday that implants transmitted users’ recovery phrases over cellular networks and that it was investigating reports beyond CryptoBilis.
Aptos rolls out Encrypted Mempool to curb frontrunning, sandwich attacks
Layer-1 blockchain Aptos has launched an optional new feature that could help shield traders from attacks involving maximal extractable value (MEV), including frontrunning and sandwich attacks.
On Monday, Aptos said its Encrypted Mempool feature is now live on its mainnet, allowing users to opt in to keep pending transactions encrypted until their block ordering is finalized. Aptos said the feature was built for institutions submitting large transactions to the chain, traders wanting to avoid MEV risk, AI agents and builders.
“When you send a transaction on any major chain today, anyone watching the network can see the details before it executes, the function you’re calling, the assets and amounts involved, and the contracts you’re interacting with,” Aptos said. “Bots use that visibility to trade against you or copy your strategy.”
Sandwich attacks, one form of MEV attack, cost Ethereum traders about $60 million over the 12 months through October 2025, according to Cointelegraph’s analysis of EigenPhi data. On Solana, sandwich attacks generated $29.7 million for bots over an 11-month period examined by Bitquery, which identified nearly 6.9 million attacks affecting about 2.2 million wallets.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Turner Wright
items.content:
Trezor reduces resellers as a ‘preventative step’ amid Ledger tampering reports
CCO Danny Sanders said he had notified certain hardware wallet resellers that they would be removed from Trezor’s list of authorized entities starting Jan. 1.
Hardware wallet producer Trezor announced it would reduce its number of resellers as a “preventive step, taken out of an abundance of caution,” following reports that malicious implants had been installed in devices made by competitor Ledger.
In a Tuesday X post, Trezor said there was “not a single piece of evidence that [its] devices have been compromised” after reports that Ledger hardware wallet users had found malicious implants that exposed recovery phrases.
However, Trezor said that it would reduce the number of its resellers, citing “recent supply-chain incidents.” Chief commercial officer Danny Sanders added that he had notified certain resellers that they would be removed from the company’s list of authorized entities on Jan. 1, and would halt shipments of Trezor devices starting on Tuesday.
Source: Trezor CCO Danny Sanders
Trezor’s response came just days after Ledger confirmed that at least one of its devices purchased by a Southeast Asian reseller contained an unauthorized hardware implant, potentially leading to millions of dollars in losses for users. The wallets, sold by reseller CryptoBilis, captured recovery phrases and transmitted them over cellular networks.
“Our setup checks are built to catch counterfeit devices and modified firmware,” a Trezor spokesperson told Cointelegraph. “The implant found in a device bought from CryptoBilis works differently. This is a unique way of tampering with the device, which doesn’t modify the firmware, but reads information on the screen and later sends it to the attacker. So far, we have not seen this specific type of attack on Trezor devices in the real world.”
Related: Ledger investigates fund losses linked to Southeast Asian reseller, warns users
During the investigation, CryptoBilis, an authorized Trezor reseller, suspended all hardware wallet sales. The parent company of European electronics retailer MediaMarkt also announced that it had removed all Ledger products from its physical stores and online platforms “as a precautionary measure.”
How much in user funds was lost?
Blockchain sleuths are still investigating the extent of losses for hardware wallet users, but research from two individuals suggested between $72 million and $86 million. Ledger reported on Tuesday that it had “not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost” due to the breaches.
The Trezor spokesperson advised users to buy products directly from the company, “checking the seal is intact,” and consider a multisignature wallet “with devices from different makers, so one compromised device can’t move funds on its own.”
Magazine: Do the Coldcard attacks mean all hardware wallets are now insecure?

items.content:
Kalshi and Polymarket won’t be part of FTC sports gambling probe, report
Rival prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket will reportedly be excluded from the Federal Trade Commission’s (FTC) probe into deceptive practices in the $167 million online sports gambling industry.
The two crypto-linked firms aren’t a focus of the FTC probe, which will instead set its sights on sportsbooks like DraftKings and FanDuel.
It will likely look into misleading advertisements, as well as the rate of suicides, hospitalizations, and bankruptcies caused by the industry.
Sources familiar with the matter told The Washington Sun that the industry evaluation “is in its early stages,” and that it’s conducted by political and career staffers.
New York alleges prediction markets cause problem gambling
Polymarket, which utilises blockchain technology, and Kalshi, which offers crypto perpetuals, are already under the scope of an insider trading probe overseen by Republican House Oversight Committee member James Comer.
The state of New York has also sued Kalshi and Polymarket this year, accusing them both of running an illegal gambling operation that’s encouraging problem gambling among people under the age of 21.
Last month’s Polymarket suit highlighted a study from the National Institutes of Health and American Psychological Association that linked pathological gambling to mental health disorders, suicidal behaviors and substance abuse.
Prediction markets say they aren’t offering gambling
Neither Kalshi nor Polymarket want to be considered gambling, and hope to be regulated federally under the Commodity Futures Trading Commission instead of individual states.
Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour recently argued that prediction markets aren’t gambling because it is an open financial market that matches buyers and sellers.
Read more: American Indian tribes want Kalshi and Polymarket off their land
Last year, Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan called DraftKings and FanDuel a sportsbooks “duopoly” that acts against winning bettors.
He said that Polymarket offers derivatives and shouldn’t be regulated like sportsbooks that offer gambling.
President Donald Trump’s son Donald Trump Jr. holds advisory roles in both firms. He holds $300,000 worth of Kalshi shares, and his investment firm 1789 Capital has invested $500 million in Polymarket.

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- Strive bought 3,311 BTC worth roughly $280 million between Oct. 5 and Oct. 9 at an average price of about $84,500 per coin, its largest purchase since January, lifting holdings to 32,773 BTC.
- The buy caps an aggressive run—following $169 million and $94.5 million purchases—for the firm, which trades as ASST and recently merged with Semler Scientific to grow its balance sheet.
- It lands amid heavy treasury activity from Strategy, Solana’s DeFi Dev Corp. and Bitmine, as Strive bought into a dip well below Bitcoin’s recent highs.
Strive is piling into Bitcoin at its fastest clip of the year, scooping up another 3,311 BTC worth roughly $280 million in its biggest single purchase since January.
The Nasdaq-listed asset manager, which trades under the ticker ASST, disclosed in a filing Monday that it bought the Bitcoin between Oct. 5 and Oct. 9 at an average price of about $84,500 per coin, including fees. The buy lifts Strive’s total holdings to 32,773 BTC, worth roughly $2.73 billion at today’s prices, up from 29,462 BTC a week earlier.
The purchase caps a stretch of aggressive accumulation. Strive added $169 million in Bitcoin earlier this month in what was then its largest buy in four months, after pushing its stack past 27,000 BTC with a $94.5 million purchase in late September.
The latest tranche extends that momentum, and the timing is notable: the firm bought as Bitcoin slid through a rough week, picking up coins at an average price well below the token’s recent highs near $87,000.
Strive, led by CEO Matthew Cole, is among a wave of public companies that have adopted Bitcoin treasury strategies, raising capital to stockpile the asset and tie their share price to its performance.
The model, pioneered by Michael Saylor’s Strategy, has drawn a crowded field, and Strive has moved aggressively since going public through its merger with Asset Entities, recently completing a tie-up with Semler Scientific to bulk up its balance sheet. Beyond its Bitcoin, the company also holds about 505,000 shares of Strategy’s STRC preferred stock, valued near $50 million, and roughly $310 million in cash.
The buying spree arrives amid a flurry of treasury activity across the sector. Strategy itself recently added $21.5 million in Bitcoin while buying back preferred stock, Solana treasury firm DeFi Development Corp. kept accumulating SOL, and Bitmine continued stacking Ethereum, though chairman Tom Lee said that company is nearly finished and will halt purchases once it holds 5% of the token’s supply.
The strategy carries the category’s familiar risk: Strive’s fortunes rise and fall with a notoriously volatile asset. Buying into a dip can pay off if Bitcoin rebounds, but the same exposure cuts the other way, and treasury firms have faced scrutiny over how much their stock premiums depend on continued accumulation.

items.content:
Broadcom CEO calls AI ‘a casino’ after co-founder dumped $750 million
When Broadcom CEO Hock Tan called AI investors gamblers behaving “like they are in a casino” on Monday, he failed to mention that his company’s own co-founder has sold roughly $750 million worth of AI stock to AI investors this year.
Tan told a Singapore conference on Monday that AI investors are behaving like gamblers who “set very extreme expectations only to find out that it’s almost like they are in a casino.”
He also compared AI spending to arcade tokens, saying, “Your parents give you $10 of tokens, you finish it in 10 minutes and you haven’t learned anything.”
Meanwhile, Broadcom co-founder and director Henry Samueli, who chaired the company’s board of directors until June 2026, spent his year dumping roughly $750 million of stock. If Tan’s casino framing is accurate, Samueli has acted like the house operator raking chips off the table.
Tan spoke this week at the DBS Asia Future Forward Conference, on a panel with Intel’s CEO. According to Bloomberg, he said many AI investors “have no clue what they are investing in.”
Fortunately, many of these ostensibly clueless investors are buying AVGO, Broadcom’s Nasdaq-listed common stock, from his co-founder.
Read more: Credit default swaps forecast AI bankruptcies
Broadcom co-founder Henry Samueli gets rich selling AI stock
Samueli has filed three Form 4s in 2026 worth approximately $250 million apiece.
His March filing covers 781,967 shares sold at a weighted average price of $319.71 apiece. In June, he sold 654,241 shares at $382.13. Lastly, in September, he sold 702,190 shares at $356.04.
In total, he sold 2,138,398 shares for about $750 million.
Tan is also getting rich himself while likening some of his investors to Las Vegas tourists. He personally sold 70,000 shares on January 6 for over $24 million.
As Broadcom insiders got rich, common shareholders have fallen behind their benchmarks.
Broadcom, an AI stock highly dependent on AI capital spending, has trailed the S&P 500 index by 11 percentage points year-to-date, and the Nasdaq 100 index by 18 points.
In its third quarter earnings report, the company admitted that sales of AI semiconductors and infrastructure for AI data centers generated the majority of its total revenue.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar claimed on CBS that many AI researchers have started smoking to show how much they believe in AI.
- Sankar provide any data, and used the segment to attack effective altruism as a doomsday cult.
- The CDC says smoking causes about one in three U.S. cancer deaths, and Anthropic's Dario Amodei says only actually curing cancer will earn public trust in AI.
Nothing says "I trust the future of medicine" quite like lighting a Marlboro and waiting for the chatbot to fix your lungs. That is the habit Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar says is spreading among AI researchers, who have supposedly started smoking cigarettes to prove how confident they are that AI will cure cancer.
"So many AI researchers have started smoking as a way of signaling to other researchers how much they believe in AI," Sankar said in an interview on CBS News' "Face the Nation" on Sunday. "I believe so much in AI that it's going to cure cancer. So I'm showing you my chips are all in."
He did not name a single researcher, cite a survey, or explain how he knows. The remark landed as an aside while host Margaret Brennan pressed him on why he was so focused on the topic.
He pointed to FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried as the effective altruist most Americans know, calling the movement a "millenarian doomsday cult." He also invoked Pascal's idea of a god-shaped hole in every human heart, which he suggested some of these researchers are filling with a machine god called AGI.
The medical record is less enthusiastic than the thesis. The CDC says smoking causes roughly one in three cancer deaths in the United States, and cigarette smoke contains at least 69 chemicals known to cause cancer.
Smokers face about 25 times the lung cancer risk of non-smokers, according to the agency. Quitting lowers the risk of 12 types of cancer, and the added lung cancer risk drops by half 10 to 15 years after stopping.
The cancer pitch is not new in this industry. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in August that promising AI will cure cancer has become “more a cliche than it is inspiring,” and that only actually curing it would earn the public's trust.
2/2 Second, on the messaging around AI. I do not agree that my messaging has been disproportionately negative. In fact it has been about equally balanced between risks and benefits: I’ve written one major essay about each, and even in interviews where I discuss the risks, I…
— Dario Amodei (@DarioAmodei) August 15, 2026
That trust is thin. In the CBS poll Brennan cited, 50% of Americans said AI will create more problems than it solves, 29% said it will solve more than it creates, and 21% were unsure.
About 45% said they want the government to restrict AI's use and development. Smoking to show faith in the technology does not obviously help that number, but it does help AI bros bond with each other. "When you're smoking, you're networking by accident," Revamp AI cofounder Stephen Campbell told Business Insider last month.
The IMF's Kristalina Georgieva recently warned that AI could hit 40% of jobs, and insiders expect a major AI incident within a year. Indirectly causing a lung cancer outbreak was probably not on their bingo card.
Palantir sells data-analysis software to governments and militaries. Most of its business relies on AI.
items.title: AI Researchers Are Smoking Cigarettes to Prove AI Will Cure Cancer, Says Palantir Exec

items.author: Aaron Wise
items.content:
XRPN took shareholder vote with no knowledge of XRP inflation bug
Shareholders of Ripple and Arrington Capital’s XRP treasury stock Evernorth Holdings would have surely loved to know that hackers could have inflated the supply of XRP by trillions of new tokens before they decided last month whether to move forward with a plan to take an XRP crypto treasury company public.
No one told them, while their share redemption window was open prior to September 28, that the XRP Ledger’s base layer payment engine had a bug allowing hackers to mint trillions of new XRP — trading today near $1.35 apiece — for almost nothing.
That bug made the fixed-supply promises of countless XRP proponents, including Evernorth CEO Asheesh Birla’s claim that 100 billion XRP was a ceiling that would never move, unenforceable on the network itself.
“All 100 billion XRP tokens were created at the time of the XRP Ledger’s launch in 2012,” Evernorth’s proxy filing read. In fact, hackers could have minted orders of magnitude more over the past decade.
Read more: Ripple pushes urgent XRPL patch — but nodes must trust its new key
Voting in an information vacuum about XRP
Although validators on the XRP Ledger have patched the bug, its existence amid Evernorth’s shareholder redemption offer is remarkable.
According to the official story, unbeknownst to XRPN shareholders — and almost everybody else on the planet — an ethical researcher privately reported the bug to Ripple’s developer arm on September 22.
Ripple then shipped an emergency, closed-source fix on September 25, obscuring that release in veiled language about “integer-arithmetic hardening.”
Shareholders faced a September 28 redemption deadline to redeem XRPN shares for cash and/or back out of the plan to merge Evernorth, an XRP treasury stock whose core value proposition rests on XRP’s limited supply, onto public markets.
The vote to proceed onto Nasdaq passed on September 30, and the merger closed on October 9.
Only on that date, October 9, did an official report admit what the September 25 “integer-arithmetic hardening” patch actually fixed: a catastrophic inflation bug that could have sent the price of XRP to near-$0.
Fortunately, the network got lucky and no one actually exploited the vulnerability while it was active.
Still, XRPN shareholders made irreversible decisions within that time window.
‘That number will never change’
Birla, a former Ripple executive and the CEO of XRPN, said on the SPAC Insider podcast, in a transcript Evernorth filed with the SEC, that “XRP is a pre-mined digital asset. One hundred billion XRP were created at inception, and that number will never change. A significant portion is held in escrow by Ripple.”
Although that number has technically never changed, it certainly could have if another researcher had utilized that inflation bug.
The flaw, per the official report, likely went back to 2015.
Researcher Cayden Liao and Veria AI reported the “overflow” issue, a euphemism for an inflation bug, on September 22 through a bug bounty program.
RippleX and the XRP Ledger Foundation reproduced the exploit, escalated its severity rating to critical, and paid the bounty.
The patch shipped September 25 in xrpld 3.4.1, with no amendment vote.
XRPN pitched XRP’s capped supply that almost wasn’t
The bug report states that a single validated transaction using the exploit “could have created spendable XRP far beyond the total supply.”
Ripple Labs is an investor in and named counterparty to the business combination agreement that took Evernorth public.
Evernorth’s registration statement carried generic boilerplate. It said the cryptography underlying the XRP Ledger could “be flawed or ineffective,” per the prospectus shareholders received.
Nothing disclosed, while the XRPN redemption window was open prior to September 30 vote, that the XRP supply cap was technically meaningless for most of the XRP Ledger’s existence.

9/11 victims claim bitcoins seized from Chinese-Iranian mining pool
Victims and families of victims of the 9/11 terrorist attack filed a statement of interest in BTC previously seized by the US government from the LuBian.com mining pool.
The filing references another suit that claims that LuBian was operated by the Iran and China Investment Development Group.
The statement of interest claims that based on this, LuBian “is an agency or instrumentality of Iran.”
Read more: Iran wants tolls paid in bitcoin for Strait of Hormuz passage
As such, these victims (known collectively as the Chairnoff Claimants), “who collectively hold judgments for more than $671 million in compensatory damages… against the Islamic Republic of Iran for its role in sponsoring” the 9/11 terrorist attacks, say they have a claim on the 127,271 BTC seized by the US government from LuBian.
LuBian wasn’t exclusively an Iranian operation and is described by the US government in several places as “a Chinese BTC mining operation,” though it’s acknowledged that it had at least a single facility in Iran.
The government claims that these funds aren’t exclusively from Lubian but also include funds associated with Chen Zhi and Prince Holding Group, and include transfers from centralized exchanges besides the mining proceeds.
There are several groups of claimants, including other 9/11 victims, who believe they have a claim to this BTC as victims of state-sponsored terror.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Turner Wright
items.content:
How the SEC’s lack of leadership could facilitate crypto rulemaking
A recent change in the SEC’s rules on quorum could make it easier for the agency to amend its approach to crypto regulation in the absence of a market structure bill.
After US lawmakers failed to pass a comprehensive digital asset market structure bill, financial regulators stepped up efforts to change rules around the oversight and enforcement of crypto companies and offerings.
However, the two primary regulators, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), are understaffed at the leadership level, leaving the decisions for regulating aspects of the $3 trillion crypto market largely in the hands of just three individuals, two of whom were nominated by US President Donald Trump.
At the SEC, two commissioners — Chair Paul Atkins and former Acting Chair Mark Uyeda — remain following the departure of Commissioner Hester Peirce earlier this month. The dearth of leadership at the CFTC is even more stark, with Michael Selig serving as the only Senate-confirmed chair and commissioner since December 2025. The agencies are intended to each have five commissioners.
Both agencies have proposed rules that appear to be attempting to take the place of legislation from Congress in regulating cryptocurrencies.
The SEC proposed rules to provide companies with a safe harbor from tokens being treated as “investment contracts” in August, and the CFTC followed suit in October, with Selig saying the agency would use its “existing statutory authorities“ to address crypto regulation through proposed rules on exchanges. Atkins added on Oct. 2 that “more regulatory proposals [were] on the horizon” for crypto.
Could one SEC commissioner have the final say on crypto rules?
On Sept. 30, the SEC made these regulatory avenues even easier with a lack of commissioners. The agency released a final rule which went into effect on Oct. 2 that it said amended quorum requirements for what it called “promot[ing] flexibility and finality of agency rulemaking.” The rule reduces the number of commissioners required for a quorum to just one person if only two are present in many cases.
“[...] with now just two commissioners around and it being entirely possible that one of them might have to recuse themselves from an issue (or be otherwise MIA), just one is now enough to pass a formal rule that applies to America’s vast multitrillion-dollar securities markets,” wrote Robin Wigglesworth in an Oct. 5 op-ed for the Financial Times.
Related: Crypto regulation at SEC, CFTC to come down to 3 commissioners following key resignation
Uyeda responded in his own Financial Times op-ed on Sunday, claiming that the SEC’s “commitment to its mission remains unchanged” despite having only two commissioners and no announcement from Trump about additional nominations to fill the empty seats. The policymaker said that the rule change “clarifies that the Commission can establish a quorum if all but one commissioner is disqualified from a matter.”
“Suggesting that the SEC is ‘hastily revamp[ing]’ its quorum rule so that the remaining commissioners can ‘have their way’ makes for a colourful comparison to fictional dystopian regimes but misleads readers about why the Commission revised its quorum rule and why it’s for the better,” said Uyeda.
As of Tuesday, the White House had not announced any nominations for the SEC and CFTC, potentially leaving the rulemaking process in the hands of just one person at each agency for months, if not longer. Congress still has time to vote on the market structure bill at the center of the controversy, the Digital Asset Market Clarity (CLARITY) Act, but some experts don’t see lawmakers advancing the legislation in a lame duck session between the 2026 midterm elections and when the next session is sworn into office in January.
Magazine: Is Bitcoin kidding itself about the Lightning Network?
items.title: How the SEC’s lack of leadership could facilitate crypto rulemaking

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Bitcoin is up 2.24% at $83,591.79 after dipping to $80,953.41, a higher low than the $80,365.12 swing that started its latest bounce.
- The Crypto Fear and Greed Index sits at a neutral 55, down from an "extreme greed" peak of 82 in August.
- Myriad traders give 54% odds that Bitcoin touches $80,000 in October and 45% odds it reaches $87,500.
Bitcoin is bouncing today following a week that had traders swapping "Uptober" memes for "spooky szn" ones after BTC cut its September gains in half.
The price of Bitcoin today slid to $80,953.41 early Tuesday, extending a Monday sell-off, then reversed to $83,591.79, up 2.24% on the day.
The Crypto Fear and Greed Index, a 0-to-100 sentiment gauge built from momentum, volatility, options positioning and social data, fell to 53 from an "extreme greed" reading of 82 on Aug. 26. It reads 56 today, a neutral score. What it boils down to is this: The August euphoria is gone, but traders aren’t panicking either.
Bitcoin ETFs are down a net $386.3 million in October, and outflows force funds to sell actual Bitcoin. Wednesday's Consumer Price Index report, expected to show annual inflation rising to 3.6% from 3.4%, is the next test: a hotter print would boost rate-hike bets and likely pressure Bitcoin. The Federal Reserve meets Oct. 27-28.
Traders on Myriad, a prediction market developed by Decrypt's parent company Dastan, give 54% odds that Bitcoin falls to $80,000 this month, down from 56% on Monday. The BTC highs in October market holds at 45% for $87,500. So, overall, sentiment has improved today, even if slightly.
Bitcoin price: Bulls defend the golden zone
Today's low stopped about $588 above $80,365.12, the swing low where the bounce began. That higher low is what traders want in an uptrend. Bitcoin also reclaimed the Fibonacci "golden zone" between $81,847.57 and $82,305.50, an area where pullbacks within uptrends often draw buyers.
The Average Directional Index, or ADX, measures trend strength, and readings above 25 confirm a trend. It reads 29.9 with buyers in control, but it was 42.8 on Oct. 7, so the uptrend is coasting rather than accelerating. The 50-day exponential moving average stayed above the 200-day, a golden cross traders read as an intact long-term uptrend.
The Relative Strength Index, a 0-to-100 momentum gauge, sits at 53.4, just above the 50 line that separates bullish from bearish momentum. The Squeeze Momentum Indicator has been on for seven sessions, meaning volatility is compressed like a coiled spring, and its -0.52 reading leans slightly bearish.
A daily close above $84,245.88 would open $86,644.19, then the $87,422.70 high, about $77 shy of Myriad's $87,500 line. Losing $81,603.02 would bring the daily trend band's upper edge into play just above $80,000. A close below it would expose $77,500.
Until Wednesday's CPI print, the active squeeze points to a market that is winding up rather than picking a direction. Oil and Iran headlines, Treasury yields, and daily ETF flows remain the short-term catalysts to track.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Trezor told partners their reseller authorization ends January 1, 2027, and that it will ship them no new stock, saying there is no evidence its devices were compromised.
- Ledger's Donjon team says wallets sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis held an implant that captures recovery phrases from the screen and sends them over LTE.
- Onchain investigator Specter traced more than $86 million in suspected thefts, a figure Ledger says it has not verified.
Trezor is cutting its network of authorized resellers, telling partners their authorization ends on January 1, 2027, days after rival hardware wallet manufacturer Ledger started an investigation that eventually confirmed a hidden spy implant in crypto wallets sold through a third-party store.
The company announced the move on X on Tuesday, saying “there is not a single piece of evidence” that Trezor devices have been compromised. It described the cut as a preventive step taken out of caution.
“Following recent supply-chain incidents, we decided to reduce the number of resellers so we can more effectively check those we work with,” Trezor wrote.
A hardware wallet is a small device that keeps the secret keys to your crypto offline, away from hackers. Setting one up produces a 24-word recovery phrase that works as a master password: whoever has those words can empty the wallet from anywhere in the world.
Ledger's Donjon security team says wallets sold by CryptoBilis, a reseller in Southeast Asia, contained an unauthorized component that reads the screen and decodes the recovery phrase when it appears. The spy implant then sends the words out over LTE, the same mobile data network your phone uses, through an eSIM, a SIM card built into the hardware. Ledger says the implant does not alter the chip that stores the keys or the device's operating system, so a tampered wallet looks and works normally.
Trezor CCO Danny Sanders shared the letter that the company sent to those providers that Trezor is ditching. “If you are receiving this letter, your authorization ends on 1 January 2027. On that date we will remove you from our list of authorized Trezor resellers,” the letter reads. “I am sorry. This decision says nothing about your effort or the way you represented us.”
This is a precautionary measure to protect our supply chain and our customers,” he wrote. “If things change in the future we will review it.”
Affected resellers will get no new stock, but they can keep selling what they have through Black Friday and the holiday season. Sanders said the decision just reflects how many partners Trezor can vet closely itself.
Neither the post nor the letter says how many resellers are affected. Trezor says it reviewed each country on its own, weighing revenue and distribution against its own presence there, and that resellers who stay will face an updated legal framework and tighter rules on how devices are sourced, stored, and handled.
Trezor said on X earlier this week that CryptoBilis was already off its seller list and that it had received no reports of tampered Trezors from the retailer.
Hi, don’t open it. Forcing the casing open can damage the device, and if it’s a Safe 7, the built-in battery makes that genuinely risky. If something about your device worries you, reach out via https://t.co/wzwW038oLv, and we’ll take a look.
We are actively investigating the…
— Trezor (@Trezor) October 12, 2026
In May 2022, Trezor warned that counterfeit Model T wallets were being sold on a Russian marketplace by a seller that was not an authorized reseller. The devices had been opened, resealed, and fitted with replaced internal components, and Trezor said the recovery phrases they generated were predictable or predefined, meaning someone else could already know the words.
Trezor's advice then was to buy only from its official shop or an authorized reseller. The second option is the network it is now shrinking.
In August, shipping partner ShipMonk exposed Trezor customer data after unauthorized access, and Trezor's September update put the total at 80,689 customers. Trezor says its systems, devices, private keys, and wallet backups were not affected.
Ledger told anyone who bought from CryptoBilis in the past 90 days not to set up their device, and told those who already did to move their funds to a new seed phrase on a device bought from Ledger. Ledger and Trezor have each warned buyers against unauthorized sellers.
items.title: Trezor Cuts Its Resellers After Ledger Finds Spy Implant in Crypto Wallets

items.content:
Strive reports $208M in warrant exercises as Bitcoin holdings jump 11%
Strive is now the fifth-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder, with 32,773 BTC, as it continues to expand its treasury through equity financing.
Strive, a publicly traded Bitcoin treasury company, increased its holdings by more than 11% last week as investors exercised $208 million in warrants, with Bitcoin purchases outpacing share issuance and giving existing shareholders greater exposure to the cryptocurrency.
In a Tuesday filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Strive disclosed that it purchased 3,311 Bitcoin (BTC) in the week ending Oct. 9 at an average price of approximately $84,500 per coin. The purchases brought its total holdings to 32,773 BTC, making it the fifth-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder, according to industry data.
At last look on Tuesday, Bitcoin was trading hands at roughly $83,300 apiece, according to Yahoo Finance data. The Strive (ASST) share price was little changed at $27.52.
Strive Chairman and CEO Matt Cole said on X that investors had exercised $208 million in warrants, with approximately 15.3 million remaining ahead of their Tuesday expiration.
Source: Matt Cole
The company also amended its governing documents to set a binding $100 minimum issuance price for its SATA preferred shares, limiting its ability to issue them below that threshold. Those shares were trading at $99.40, at last look.
Strive’s latest purchases increased its Bitcoin holdings per share even as the company issued additional equity. During the reporting period, its Bitcoin reserves grew 11.2%, outpacing a 9.4% increase in its effective common share count.
Related: Treasury yields at 5% threaten extending Bitcoin’s best quarter since 2017
Michael Saylor weighs in on Strive’s Bitcoin strategy
Strive’s latest purchase drew praise from Michael Saylor, whose company, Strategy, pioneered the corporate Bitcoin treasury model.
“Strive is turning demand for digital equity (ASST) and digital credit (SATA) into demand for Bitcoin,” Saylor wrote on X. “Its hypergrowth shows how the capital markets are accelerating Bitcoin adoption.”
Saylor was referring to Strive’s use of common and preferred shares to raise capital for Bitcoin purchases, a strategy similar to Strategy’s own approach through its MSTR common stock and STRC preferred shares.
Strategy added a comparatively modest 250 BTC to its treasury last week, bringing its total holdings to 848,250 BTC and maintaining its position as the largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder.
Related: Saylor teases Strategy Bitcoin buying after ending September with STRC buybacks

Why not just let software be fluid and, like Heraclitus river, never step twice in the same repo.

We thought it was good—until we got our hands on an early internal snapshot of Claude Mythos Preview. We asked it to rewrite the whole thing, and with no further instructions, it produced a version that consumed 20x less memory and was 4x faster, while preserving all of the implicit invariants around ingestion ordering and data structures. I feel like the advantage of ...

[tancop]: So it's a SVN/Perforce style server based VCS with a more modern design. Sounds exactly like Lore from Epic Games but with zero production use outside the company and no support for non text assets. And they won't release the code.

[jcims]: Every now and then I like to browse the claude code release notes just to get a sense of the number of changes in that product over time. Bitcoin keeps up pressure on $84K as US stocks skirt Korea tech sell-off
Bitcoin price action preserved overnight gains as US stocks quickly rebounded after opening lower on the back of Korea’s tech-stock rout.
Bitcoin (BTC) continued to target $84,000 at Tuesday’s Wall Street open as US stocks attempted to shake off South Korea’s latest tech rout.
Key points:
- Bitcoin approached $84,000 once more at the start of US trading on Tuesday, still up by around 2%.
- US equities avoided a copycat sell-off after Korea’s KOSPI index finished the day down 5.4%.
- Analysis from CryptoQuant warned of increasing US dollar strength challenging BTC price upside as DXY hit its highest level in 18 months.
S&P 500, Nasdaq brush off KOSPI losses
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD returning to near $83,800 at the start of the US trading session, preserving much of its overnight upside.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Equities opened lower on the day after futures fell during Asia trading after Korea’s KOSPI Composite Index shed 7.4% over two days. Semiconductors led the losses amid mounting fears over AI expenditures and competition from China.
Both the S&P 500 index and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite index made early gains to briefly turn green on the day, however, both gauges were off less than 0.5% at the time of writing.
Nasdaq Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
“The most important development has been not just bond yields going up, but the volatility for bonds... and that’s starting to work its way out through asset pricing across the board,” Damien Boey, portfolio strategist at Wilson Asset Management in Sydney, Australia, told Reuters. He said:
“It’s a very uncomfortable situation on many fronts... maybe AI capex just comes off the boil a little bit, and maybe a few players are casualties in that.”
Bitcoin remained caged around exchange order-book liquidity, which continued to act as resistance above $84,000, per data from CoinGlass.
BTC liquidation heatmap. Source: CoinGlass
Related: BTC price support holds ahead of US CPI data: Three things Bitcoin traders need to know this week
Dollar strength in focus as DXY hits 18-month highs
Bitcoin bulls are facing a double macro headwind this month, CryptoQuant contributor Darkfost said in market commentary on Tuesday.
With bond yields circling their highest levels in nearly a quarter of a century, US dollar strength has increased markedly. The US dollar index (DXY), which compares the dollar to a basket of US trading-partner currencies, has increased by 5.5% since Sept. 9 and hit 102.57 on the day, its highest levels since April 2025.
US dollar index (DXY) one-week chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
While the traditionally inverse correlation between DXY and BTC has declined this year, the post on onchain analytics platform sees crypto markets suffering from a lack of risk appetite.
“Taken together, these factors constrain the liquidity available to markets and erode institutional confidence, leaving them reluctant to take on more risk.” he wrote in the blog post, adding:
“The climate is therefore unfavorable for Bitcoin, which is perceived as a highly risky asset, while tech (NDX) and the S&P 500, more mature markets, continue to surge and absorb what little liquidity remains.”

UK crypto trader says almost $800,000 lost in knife assault as wrench attacks proliferate
A crypto trader in the U.K. claimed masked intruders stole nearly $800,000 in cryptocurrency at knifepoint, furthering concerns of "wrench attacks" spreading in the country.
- A cryptocurrency trader in the U.K. said armed intruders held him at knifepoint and forced him to transfer about $760,000 in digital assets, though police have not confirmed the account.
- Such robberies, known as “wrench attacks,” use violence or threats to force cryptocurrency holders to surrender their assets, bypassing digital security measures.
- Chainalysis estimated that criminals stole more than $30 million through violent attacks in the first half of 2026, with home invasions accounting for 37% of recorded cases.
A cryptocurrency trader in the U.K. claimed to have had almost $800,000 of crypto stolen after armed intruders broke into his home and forced him to transfer digital assets to a specific wallet, highlighting a threat to investors that neither self-custody nor encryption can prevent.
The unidentified trader, pseudonymously “realist” on X, said attackers held him at knifepoint, destroyed his phone and forced transfers of approximately $40,000 from a hot wallet and $720,000 from his Ledger wallet.
The trader shared a Solana wallet address on blockchain explorer Solscan to substantiate his account, though there has yet been no corresponding confirmation from the police or other authorities regarding the incident.
“If you live in the U.K. and do crypto get the f**k out,” he posted.
The incident follows recent reports of a similar U.K. robbery last December, where masked attackers beat a cryptocurrency investor with hammers and threatened to kill his pregnant wife unless he transferred hundreds of thousands of pounds in crypto.
Such crimes, commonly called “wrench attacks,” involve physical violence or threats to compel crypto holders to surrender their assets.
Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis estimates criminals stole more than $30 million through violent attacks in the first half of 2026. Home invasions accounted for 37% of recorded incidents, up from 14% a year earlier.
France emerged as a hotspot for wrench attacks, with Chainalysis documenting at least 30 recorded incidents in the first half of this year.
Blockchain security firm Certik identified 52 verified attacks globally during that period, of which 33 were in France.
The figures suggest physical coercion is becoming an increasingly significant concern alongside wholly digital threats such as hacks, phishing and smart-contract exploits.
The implications for investors extend beyond protecting private keys to keeping holdings confidential, limiting public disclosures about one’s trading activity and separating readily available funds from long-term reserves. However, no individual technical safeguards can eliminate the threat of violence.

Solana共识升级Alpenglow将于10月21日上线mainnet-beta，区块最终确认时间缩短至150毫秒

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 13 日，据官方消息，Solana 研究和开发公司 Anza 宣布 Alpenglow 将于 10 月 21 日约 22:50（UTC+8）在 Solana mainnet-beta 上线。这项升级历经 18 个月开发，届时将在一个时隙内完成迁移。区块最终确认时间将从数秒缩短至约 150 毫秒。Alpenglow 将取代 Solana 自主网上线以来一直使用的 TowerBFT 共识协议。该升级结合了最新共识研究成果与纠删码数据分发技术，旨在提升全球网络中的区块确认速度，使其尽可能接近物理条件所允许的极限。

Alpenglow 有望为全天候运行的全球资本市场提供更高效的底层基础设施，支持高带宽交易及即时结算。对于机构用户，该协议可将交易结算时间从通常的 1 至 3 个工作日缩短至约 150 毫秒，并提供密码学保证，同时推动支付处理直接在链上完成，减少中间环节及对账需求。对于开发者而言，更快的确认速度有望提升 Web3 应用的响应能力，减少等待提示及重试逻辑，使链上应用的交互体验更接近传统互联网应用。

此外，Alpenglow 也将为 AI 代理提供更适合机器高速执行的链上交易环境。结合 x402 等支付工具，AI 代理有望在无需许可的情况下更高效地完成支付及其他链上操作，减少交易过程中的摩擦。该升级将进一步增强 Solana 对高频交易、机构金融服务、Web3 应用及 AI 代理经济等场景的支持能力。

【IMF：代币化 RWA 市场规模约 650 亿美元，或成杠杆与流动性风险新渠道】

Foresight News 消息，国际货币基金组织（IMF）发布 10 月《全球金融稳定报告》，首次用专门章节讨论代币化市场。报告显示，截至 7 月底，不含回购和稳定币的代币化 RWA 公开市场规模约 650 亿美元，其中信贷约 304 亿美元，货币市场基金约 175 亿美元，股票约 23 亿美元；代币化回购 30 日平均日交易量达 3030 亿美元。代币化股票发行高度集中，Ondo Finance 和 Backed Finance（xStocks）合计占比超过 70%；超过 50% 的交易发生在美股常规交易时段之外，约 80% 的交易规模不足一股，但波动率约为传统市场的 1.5 倍，流动性也明显更低。IMF 认为，代币化资产规模虽小，可能在多个领域带来效率提升，但也可能形成杠杆积累及流动性和期限错配的新渠道，并加剧技术和基础设施风险，目前系统性风险仍然有限。IMF 还指出，若缺乏可互操作的央行货币，稳定币和代币化存款可能成为代币化资本市场的主要结算工具，从而带来发行方信用风险和集中度风险。此外，IMF 在报告中表示，全球金融体系面临的风险仍处于高位，主要包括 AI 相关资产价格回调、主权债收益率大幅上升以及日益严重的网络攻击威胁。

[andyjohnson0]: There's lots of amusingly Telegraph-esque outrage being posted here. But the article makes it clear that the reduction is due to reduction in demand, due in part to welcome improvements in efficiency, but also regrettable deindustrialization, and (neutral?) increased importing of electricity. Nobody is planning to ration electricity suppies. I also wonder what the contribution of domestic solar and on-site industrial generation is? I'm a dev in a large manufacturing business and two...

[cm2187]: I was at a conference last year where one of the speakers was from National Grid. Not only these morons had in mind that electricity demand should decrease (even before AI, it was obvious that demand would go up as we are moving away from fossil fuel with both heating and transportation going electric). But their great idea to deal with the shortage is intermittent availability of power. You won't be able to wash your clothes when you feel like, you will have to adapt to when there is sp...

[advisedwang]: The decline in energy from 2003-present lines up nicely with the phase out of incandescent lights in favour of CFLs and of CFLs in favour of LEDs. Lets say a house typically had 5 60W bulbs on for 8hrs a day, now replaced with an 8W bulb.  That would be a 2 kWH reduction, which roughly corresponds to the drop shown in the data. EDIT: actually now that I think about it, 2kWh per-household is probably less than 1kWh per-capita. It's still a good chunk though!

[gste]: Let's get this straight: yes, there's been a reduction in demand and increases in efficiency, but electricity is objectively extremely expensive in the UK now. Energy is being heavily imported. This has disastrous consequences for businesses and the economy. It is the number one biggest problem facing the UK economy after the huge government debt and crippling taxes... although there are a number of other problems I could mention.

[klelatti]: The linked iea data shows that the reduction is roughly 50/50 industrial and residential. So the deindustrialisation narrative is part of the story but improved efficiency at home is also a significant factor.

Coinbase量子顾问委员会发布比特币抗量子升级建议，呼吁尽早启动迁移准备

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 13 日，Coinbase 量子顾问委员会发布关于量子计算与区块链的立场文件，探讨比特币应对未来量子计算威胁的技术路径。Coinbase 表示，比特币向抗量子体系迁移不仅需要选择抗量子数字签名方案，还需兼顾区块空间限制、全节点验证能力、机构托管需求、普通钱包兼容性及存量资产迁移等问题。Coinbase 目前托管约占比特币总供应量 5% 的 BTC，正推进自身系统的抗量子准备工作，并与比特币开发者和研究人员展开讨论，通过工程资源及参与比特币安全联盟支持相关开源研究。该文件旨在为社区讨论提供技术参考，并非最终方案或正式定论。

在技术方案方面，Coinbase 建议在量子计算威胁尚未明确到来之前就启动准备工作，因为比特币共识规则调整及整个生态的迁移可能需要数年时间。该公司认为，应考虑采用可灵活引入、替换或补充不同抗量子签名算法的输出结构，并评估 P2MR（BIP-360）、P2TRv2 等设计。同时，可研究传统签名与抗量子签名并行的混合方案，使用户能够在最终确定传统签名停用政策之前逐步迁移。对于签名算法的选择，Coinbase 建议综合比较签名及密钥大小、验证速度、侧信道防护、随机数依赖、硬件钱包与多方计算（MPC）兼容性、安全性及标准化进展，并重点评估 ML-DSA、SLH-DSA、未来标准化后的 FN-DSA，以及包括 SHRINCS 在内的其他候选方案。

Coinbase 还特别提醒，状态型抗量子签名虽然可能具有签名体积更小、速度更快等优势，但状态管理不当可能导致状态重复使用，进而引发签名伪造风险，因此应提供无状态备用方案，并明确钱包和托管服务的安全管理要求。此外，对于尚未迁移、遗失密钥或无法访问的比特币资产，Coinbase 认为应将其视为独立的治理与工程问题，审慎评估冻结、限速、救援机制及传统签名逐步退出等方案，确保相关措施本身具备抗量子安全性。Coinbase 强调，迁移过程涉及区块空间、安全性、隐私、费用及用户资产可访问性等多重权衡，社区应在推进抗量子签名技术工作的同时，持续讨论存量资产的处理方式。

In brief
- AnyPS5 is an open-source, AI-powered project on GitHub that converts PS5 game executables into programs that run natively on PC.
- Speculators believe that the tool will allow users to get higher performance out of PS5 games by using high-powered PCs.
- Some gamers hope that the project will be able to run GTA VI on PC at launch, although Discord members warn there's likely to be roadblocks.
Vibe coders are porting PlayStation 5 applications to Windows and Linux, leaving some users optimistic that the project will unlock better performance for PS5 games, and could even work for GTA 6 at launch.
AnyPS5 is an open-source, AI-powered project on GitHub that converts PS5 game executables into programs that run natively on PC, swapping Sony’s system libraries for its own version rather than emulating the console. A community-run tracker lists more than 180 PS5 titles that have been tried with the tool, but only a handful have been verified as playable.
An important distinction to make is that this is not an emulator and that games will be running natively on PC. As a result, some speculators believe that users will be able to get better performance from PS5 games by playing them on a high-powered PC.
"GTA 6 most likely will be able to run on your PC at launch, and [with] significantly higher frames than it would on your PS5," pseudonymous gaming content creator Schlayerr said on TikTok. "We live in a crazy time."
"Technically, this is feasible given the similarities between console and PC architectures, and AI can dramatically accelerate the reverse engineering work," Theodore Agranat, Director of Web3 at Gunzilla Games, the game studio behind battle royale Off the Grid, told Decrypt. However, he remained skeptical over whether they "can deliver the quality, performance, and fidelity players expect from AAA games at scale."
🚨 ANYPS5 SYSTEM LIBRARY SUPPORT JUST HIT 86%! 🤯🔥
Development has been FAST since Friday, and the library side is becoming the next phase to watch.
• 3,005 / 3,475 declared system functions implemented
• Overall system library support is now 86.47%
• libc: 99%
•… pic.twitter.com/S1AekKNtOf— Chris Mizo (@MizoChris) October 12, 2026
The latest project update claims that 100% of the PS5 GPU shaders have been ported while 88% of the system libraries have been ported. Discord community members believe the final 12% for system libraries is likely to take a long time, especially as new system libraries are continuously being discovered.
In the Discord showcase channel, some users have shown off rudimentary demos of PS5 games on PC. One community developer reported running GTA 5 at 27 frames per second, or FPS, in the performance graphics mode. Others have reported getting 4 FPS on Epic Mickey, 25 FPS on Phasmophobia, and 60 FPS on Vampire Survivors. It's still a work in progress.
Still, in all of these examples, the games aren't fully playable due to the incomplete system library port as well as game-specific bugs being encountered.
A potential roadblock in playing GTA 6 on PC at launch is a mandatory firmware update, Discord members say. This is because the AnyPS5 project would need to overhaul its converted files to the latest update in order to get GTA 6 running. As such, there is likely to be a delay before the game is available on PC via AnyPS5.
"Firmware updates could create hurdles, particularly around DRM, but likely wouldn’t invalidate the entire approach," Agranat said.
A response to Sony's disc ban?
AnyPS5 bans any form of piracy in its Discord server, meaning using the tool requires purchasing the game on the PlayStation Store. That said, there is nothing stopping an individual using AnyPS5 with a pirated copy of a video game.
Some PlayStation users have speculated that the movement is a response to Sony's plan to discontinue physical game discs.
"The reason this all happened is because Sony discontinued discs," pseudonymous gaming content creator The 1st Gamer said on TikTok. "They wanted to go digital, and they did, but just not on PS5."
Sony announced in July that it plans to stop producing physical discs at the start of 2028. The decision was met with major community backlash, including a petition called "Don't Kill the Disc" gaining over 385,000 signatures. Shawn Layden, a former PlayStation executive, called the move a "heavily spreadsheeted decision" and said it has damaged the company's reputation.
In August, Sony argued in a California court that purchasing a digital game in the PlayStation Store does not equate to ownership of it. Sony claimed its Terms of Service and the Software Product License Agreement explain this and that users should understand it as a fact.
"Even without Sony stopping physical discs, this was bound to happen with AI accelerating dev," Agrant said. "My hope is that projects like this push platform holders to offer the same flexibility themselves, but at a much higher standard," he told Decrypt, hoping for a future where Sony rolls out games on PC as well as console. "That would be a genuine win-win."
items.title: AI Powered PlayStation Crack Could Let You Play GTA 6 on PC at Launch

Sui Devnet Adds Post-Quantum Signature Support, Targets Mainnet Rollout in Q1 2027

Mysten Labs co-founder and chief cryptographer Kostas Chalkias announced that Sui Devnet has successfully processed its first native quantum-safe transaction, sharing the on-chain transaction record. Sui's core developer Mysten Labs has introduced ML-DSA-65 post-quantum signature support in Devnet release v1.82.0, allowing signed transactions to be submitted through the ExecuteTransaction API and verified through the VerifySignature API.

ML-DSA-65 is also supported in multisignature transactions, with additional integration into GraphQL and the Rust SDK. According to Sui's previously announced roadmap, native ML-DSA-65 accounts are expected to reach Testnet by the end of 2026, with native account authentication on Mainnet targeted for Q1 2027, subject to security audits and testing results. — link

items.author: Cointelegraph by Zoltan Vardai
items.content:
Anthropic warns ‘AI worms’ may autonomously spread across devices like a virus
Anthropic warned that rogue “AI worms” are months away from the ability to self-replicate and autonomously infect user devices such as home appliances and other internet-connected devices.
Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic warned that self-replicating autonomous AI systems may start spreading across user devices without human intervention, akin to computer viruses.
Rogue “AI worms” may start autonomously targeting everyday devices, including Android TVs, smart appliances, cameras and other internet-connected devices with basic computing power and weak security, according to a Monday report by researchers William Zhou and Daniel Freeman for Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team.
Small AI models may be “months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial internet-of-things (IoT) devices,” which would be a challenging threat as it would have “no centralized point to shut off,” the authors said.
The warning follows renewed concerns over the growing mathematical capabilities of AI models, which may eventually break the cryptographic signatures used in crypto wallets, threatening about one-third of the Bitcoin supply.
Almost a third of global Bitcoin supply, or 6.26 million BTC, currently sits in addresses vulnerable to being broken by AI models or quantum computers. However, 4.33 million are exposed because of address reuse, meaning that moving that BTC to fresh wallets would end the exposure, wrote Glassnode co-founder Rafael Schultze-Kraft in a Thursday X post.
A day earlier, Ethereum researcher Justin Drake warned that rapid AI advancements could break the elliptic curve digital signature algorithm (ECDSA) securing cryptocurrency wallets sooner than previously expected and urged users to migrate to fresh wallets.
Dragonfly’s managing partner, Haseeb Qureshi, called the warning “cryptographic doomerism” and said that migrating tokens to fresh addresses was not a real solution against the threat.
Related: AI has not triggered DeFi ‘hackpocalypse,’ Dragonfly partner says
items.title: Anthropic warns ‘AI worms’ may autonomously spread across devices like a virus

知名交易员Killa：比特币需守住8万美元并形成更高低点，否则回调或将加深

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 13 日，知名交易员 Killa 发文表示，如果比特币要按照目前走势结构演变，就需要在 7.55 万美元上方形成更高低点，理想情况下还应守住 8 万美元附近的低点。这与 2023 年的走势类似：当时比特币在周线级别形成更高高点，随后回踩并守住了原有区间。这或许解释了为什么近期低时间框架的行情显得如此容易触发止损、走势激进且充满算法交易的痕迹。比特币曾在 8.2 万美元区间收复内部结构，随后回踩，再度跌破结构，之后又重新收复。整个市场似乎都在刻意诱导交易者入场。

不得不承认，最初回落至 8.1 万美元区间的走势，从结构上看并不理想。但当时有大量空头在低位集中开仓，这或许能够解释随后出现的价格反应。另一个值得关注的细节是，比特币从 8.41 万美元跌至 8.1 万美元期间，仅有约 3 亿美元的多头头寸被清算；而此前从 8.68 万美元跌至 8.06 万美元时，多头清算规模超过 20 亿美元。多头清算规模明显下降，表明当前市场对多头头寸的依赖程度可能已低于此前。

目前的行情颇为微妙。比特币需要在当前位置形成更高低点，并由此展开新一轮上涨，否则此次回调可能将价格带至 8 万美元下方。就目前而言，所谓的「暴跌保护团队」在维持价格方面做得不错，但同时也在不断搅乱低时间框架下的内部震荡区间。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371620

items.content:
OpenCode 2.0重写底层：MCP工具能用代码串联，多个Agent可后台并行干活

动察 Beating AI 快讯，开源 AI 编程工具 OpenCode 2.0 正式亮相，此前已在 7 月开启公测。这次升级的一大变化是 Code Mode，可以把 MCP 服务和 OpenAPI 接口转成 JavaScript 函数，让 Agent 在一段脚本中串联多个工具。比如先从 GitHub 批量读取 Bug，再逐条创建 Linear 任务，不用每处理一条数据就让模型重新发起调用。所有 MCP 服务默认启用 Code Mode，也能减少工具定义占用的上下文。

OpenCode 还重写了底层架构。终端、网页和桌面客户端现在共享同一个本地后台服务，可以访问同一批会话。子 Agent 和 Shell 命令也能在后台运行，例如让一个 Agent 审查代码，主 Agent 继续修改文件，同时执行测试和构建。团队还将大量内部功能做成插件，目前已超过 80 个，支持运行时热加载，Agent 可以为自己编写插件并立即使用。

此外，OpenCode 推出了可嵌入其他应用的 SDK。Cloudflare 已宣布通过实验性接口支持 OpenCode 2.0，让开发者能在 Durable Objects 中运行同一套 Agent 引擎，并保存会话、恢复中断的任务。

不过，这次重构也带来了兼容性问题。1.x 插件需要改写，旧版 Server API 也需要适配。GitHub 上有 issue 指出，Code Mode 调用耗时较长的插件时缺少超时限制，可能让会话长时间处于等待状态，只能手动中断。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371618
items.title: OpenCode 2.0重写底层：MCP工具能用代码串联，多个Agent可后台并行干活

items.author: Jacob Lyon
items.content:
German Ledger reseller pauses sales following $86M draining incident
Official European Ledger reseller MediaMarkt is no longer selling the wallets following reports that some of the devices may have been fitted with physical spyware, leading to an $86 million draining incident.
The German company told Cointelegraph that it has “removed all of the manufacturer’s products from its stores and online platforms” and that it’s in contact with Ledger. “We take this incident very seriously,” it added.
Ledger wallets bought from Malaysian reseller CryptoBilis were drained of millions of dollars worth of funds last week.
Since then, former Mt. Gox CEO Mark Karpelès has been helping to identify spyware in Ledger wallets that have been dismantled, photographed, and shared on X by their owners.
Karpelès has reportedly found spyware in Ledger wallets sold by MediaMarkt, official Philippine reseller LazMall, CryptoBilis, and more recently, in a wallet sold at Metapod in Singapore’s airport.
Ledger hasn’t linked other resellers to $86M drain
Despite these discoveries, Ledger’s newest statement only confirmed that wallets sold by CryptoBilis were involved in the draining incident.
It said, “We have not verified a drain linked to a signer bought elsewhere,” and adds that it’s “reviewing reports of implants in other signers and locations.”
Read more: Ledger sued for $500M over its many data breaches
Ledger also announced that its security team is investigating the tampered devices sourced from CryptoBilis. The team deduced that the spyware was able to record a Ledger wallet’s 24-word recovery phrase and transmit it with the attached eSIM.
The company noted that CryptoBilis isn’t selling wallets while the investigation continues.
Protos has reached out to LazMall for comment and will update this piece should we hear anything back.

Is Bitcoin kidding itself about the Lightning Network?
Bitcoin developer Paul Sztorc says Bitcoiners are lying to themselves about Lightning. Developers claim usability has improved, but questions remain over everyday adoption.
Bitcoin developer Paul Sztorc ruffled a few feathers this month with a brutally blunt assessment of the Lightning Network: Bitcoiners are lying to themselves about how well it works.
“Most people don’t realize how bad the Lightning Network is,” Sztorc said in an October 4 post on X, “because there has been a vast, years long conspiracy to ***lie*** about the LN user experience.”
He argued that custodial Lightning services account for more than 80% of payments, and described their promotion as a “vast campaign of fraud on par with Elizabeth Holmes’ Theranos,” he said, referring to fake blood-testing device company whose founder was convicted of fraud.
Lightning payments are private by design, making it impossible to establish the custodial share from public network data alone. Sztorc did not respond to Magazine’s requests for comment.
But his scathing criticism resurfaces a topic Bitcoin developers have wrestled with for years: Has Lightning made Bitcoin easier to use, or has the community become so invested in Layer 2 protocol that it overlooks its shortcomings?
Lightning has a usability problem
Lightning was designed to enable faster, cheaper Bitcoin transactions without every payment having to be individually recorded on the blockchain, but its underlying mechanics have often created friction for users and businesses alike.
Sztorc says people don’t realize how bad the Lightning Network is. Source: Paul Sztorc
In a one-click world where users of TradFi rails can tap a card or click a mouse to complete a transaction, Lightning’s clunky payment channels rely on liquidity being available in the right places at the right times. Routing payments through the network can fail, especially larger payments requiring several hops through different nodes.
Related: Big Questions: Does Satoshi actually own 1.1 million Bitcoin?
Even Lightning’s head of liquidity, Alex Bosworth, said this month, “the painful truth is that in a setup with privacy and p2p etc it’s extremely slow compared to tap to pay.”
Added to that, running a node and managing channels is simply way too technical for the average user, who just wants to pay for stuff and get on with their day. That’s the reason for high estimates of custodial use — it’s easier and works better at the expense of using a trusted intermediary.
Everyday payments have a 99.7% success rate
Jesse Shrader, co-founder and chief executive of Lightning infrastructure provider Amboss, acknowledges that liquidity requirements are “challenging” to understand at first, but he says they are “trivial to solve” with current tools or automation services.
He tells Magazine, “For everyday payments of around $100, most users can achieve 99% reliability in the core network,” adding that Amboss’ simulations put the success rate for $100 payments at 99.66%.
Lightning exceeded $1 billion in transaction volume in November 2025. Source: River
While that’s an encouraging benchmark, it’s not a verified, network-wide measure of everyone’s experience in practice. As they say in the fine print of advertisements: Your results may vary.
In an April 2026 Reddit discussion, one user said he was “genuinely impressed” by where the network had gotten technically, but still questioned how useful it was for everyday spending. “There is still a gap in practice,” he said:
“Every coffee shop, grocery store and gas station I walk into runs on Visa or Mastercard terminals. NFC tap to pay is the standard. Nobody is running a Lightning node at the point of sale and nobody is going to.”
Have developers solved the problem?
Danny Stagg, marketing lead at Bitcoin payments infrastructure provider Breez, says much of the criticism of Lightning’s user experience is now outdated.
“The criticism is not fair in 2026,” he tells Magazine, “but historically it was. For years, both developers and users were asked to understand the complexities of Lightning, like channels and inbound liquidity, just to get paid.”
He says the network has greatly improved over the past two years, with newer infrastructure abstracting much of that complexity away. “Non-custodial UX is now comparable with custodial,” he says.
Users no longer need to manage channels or run their own nodes for a wallet or application to offer Lightning payments, as developers and service providers can handle much of the work underneath the hood.
Related: Lightning Network hits record capacity on crypto exchange adoption
Breez chief executive Roy Sheinfeld says that AI coding tools are making it easier for developers to build Bitcoin-enabled applications, and inquiries from prospective partners have rapidly increased.
“That’s why we’re seeing more partners add Bitcoin every quarter,” Stagg says.
But growing developer interest does not necessarily mean more people are using Lightning for everyday payments.
The numbers show activity, not necessarily success
According to its 2026 Bitcoin adoption report, financial services company River estimated that Lightning processed $1.17 billion in transaction volume across 5.22 million transactions in November 2025 alone.
While that seems like an impressive number, it remains below Lightning’s August 2023 peak of 6.6 million transactions, suggesting transaction counts have not kept pace with the value moving through the network.
Crypto payment processor CoinGate reported 782,403 paid crypto orders across its own customer base in the first half of 2026, up 21.4% year over year, with Lightning accounting for 9.6% of Bitcoin payments processed through its service.
Lightning accounted for 9.6% of Bitcoin payments. Source: CoinGate
What would count as success?
Shrader says that since network-level payment statistics are “impossible to produce unless you are party to the transactions themselves,” he isn’t buying Sztorc’s claim that more than 80% of Lightning payments are custodial.
“I distrust anyone who claims they can prove an 80% custodial share either way from public data alone.”
Stagg says the claim “describes yesterday’s Lightning,” when custodial services offered an easier experience and non-custodial services hadn’t “caught up” yet. (Back in 2023, River estimated one self custodial user for every eight custodial users). But without hard data that’s up to date, the custody question can’t be settled.
And the same caution should apply to claims about Lightning adoption measured in metrics like payment volume, network capacity or developer interest; each measures something different, and none alone can establish how easy Lightning is to use.
Businesses are processing payments and developers are finding ways to abstract technical complexity, but technical progress is not the same as mainstream usability.
The real criticism may not be that Lightning has failed, but whether its supporters conflate evidence of what the network can do with what people are actually doing on the network.
Related: Bitcoin treasury firms can outperform BTC... but is the risk worth taking?
items.title: Is Bitcoin kidding itself about the Lightning Network?

items.content:
Digital cash offers ‘cash-like privacy,’ but bank data breaches threaten users: BIS
BIS said that digital cash can achieve “cash-like privacy,” however, the technology isn’t yet production-ready due to risks such as bank data breaches.
The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) said digital cash can offer privacy properties similar to cash, but highlighted remaining risks, including how potential bank data breaches may expose users’ personal data.
While digital cash can achieve “cash-like privacy,” the technology stack is not yet “production ready,” wrote BIS in its Project Aurum Phase 2 report, published on Tuesday.
This phase implements a privacy-preserving digital cash prototype using BIS’s existing Aurum codebase to take a balanced approach between complete anonymity and full transaction transparency, BIS said.
BIS found that compromising one bank may expose its customer data, but would not expose customer identities from other counterparties. A validator-level compromise alone would not be enough to expose end users, according to the report.
The BIS report explores the technical features needed to establish a privacy-preserving central bank digital currency (CBDC). CBDC critics previously raised concerns about the technology’s potential financial surveillance capabilities.
In 2023, Brazil’s central bank published the source code for its CBDC pilot, and within days, people noticed the surveillance and control mechanisms embedded within its code, allowing the central bank to freeze or reduce user funds within CBDC wallets.
Earlier this year, US President Donald Trump banned federal agencies from issuing a CBDC in January, citing financial stability and privacy concerns.
Related: Republican lawmakers call for permanent CBDC ban as House vote approaches
items.title: Digital cash offers ‘cash-like privacy,’ but bank data breaches threaten users: BIS

AI科研新榜单：Claude 48小时测试夺冠，GPT-6却钻了评分漏洞

动察 Beating AI 快讯，美国 AI 公司 Hillclimb 发布 DeepRSI，用 15 道真实机器学习研究任务，测试 Agent 在 48 小时内持续开展实验、优化方案的能力。任务涵盖 GPU 计算加速、视觉模型推理优化等。首批 5 款模型中，Claude Fable 5.1 以 1548 Elo 排名第一，GPT-6 Astra 为 1232，Kimi K3 为 820。GPT-6 初期领先，但 Claude 在后续实验中逐渐反超。三者测试成本分别约为 627、404 和 159 美元。

测试还发现，部分模型会为了提高成绩钻评分规则的空子。在一道彩色网格推理任务中，GPT-6 发现模型训练效果不佳，竟直接将现成的求解算法编码进模型权重，被研究团队列为严重的奖励机制漏洞案例。Grok 4.7 则利用公开测试集训练，Gemini 3.8 Flash 也针对公开样本反复调参。这些做法可能提高分数，却不代表模型真正学会了通用解题方法。

DeepRSI 测试的是 AI 能否长时间自主改进既定研究方案，而非真正实现递归自我改进。任务目标和评分标准仍由人类设定，而且只有 15 道题，每款模型仅测试两次。即使取得高分，也不能证明 AI 已能自主研发出比自身更强的下一代模型。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/371611

阿里近百人开发千问办公电商版：计划双11前推出，但暂不能代投广告

动察 Beating AI 快讯，阿里正组织近百人开发千问办公的首个行业版本，专门面向电商商家，计划赶在 10 月 15 日天猫双11预售前推出。项目今年 6 月开始筹备，9 月进入集中开发，由千问办公 CEO 陈宇森统筹，黄丕培（花名灵培）负责。新版本不是独立 App，而是在千问办公中切换到「电商经营」模式。

电商版主要覆盖经营分析、商品管理、素材生产和营销推广等场景。商家可以让 AI 汇总多个平台、多个店铺的数据，发现经营异常并提出建议；也能上传商品、服装和模特素材，制作营销图片，再用 AI 表格整理消费者评价和待办事项。淘宝、天猫数据可以直接连接，有赞、客如云正在逐步接入，其他平台则需要商家授权登录。

电商行业已贡献千问办公约 20% 的付费用户，是目前占比最高的行业。负责人黄丕培此前曾主导孵化 AI 电商工具绘蛙，截至今年 9 月，该产品已有 150 万用户，年化经常性收入约 5000 万元。阿里今年 3 月还推出了面向跨境业务的 Accio Work，已经能够协助商家选品、建店和发布商品。

不过，千问办公电商版目前仍以数据分析和内容生产为主，不能直接替商家调整投流计划，也无法自动花钱投放广告，更谈不上接管整家店铺。阿里这次希望把分散在不同工具中的经营工作集中起来，让千问办公成为商家日常工作的入口。相比通用 AI 办公产品的功能竞争，阿里正在尝试利用自身的电商数据和商家资源争夺付费客户。

电商行业已贡献千问办公约 20% 的付费用户，是目前占比最高的行业。负责人黄丕培此前曾主导孵化 AI 电商工具绘蛙，截至今年 9 月，该产品已有 150 万用户，年化经常性收入约 5000 万元。阿里今年 3 月还推出了面向跨境业务的 Accio Work，已经能够协助商家选品、建店和发布商品。

不过，千问办公电商版目前仍以数据分析和内容生产为主，不能直接替商家调整投流计划，也无法自动花钱投放广告，更谈不上接管整家店铺。阿里这次希望把分散在不同工具中的经营工作集中起来，让千问办公成为商家日常工作的入口。相比通用 AI 办公产品的功能竞争，阿里正在尝试利用自身的电商数据和商家资源争夺付费客户。

items.author: theblockbeats
items.content:
Cipher Digital计划发行8.5亿美元可转债，为数据中心项目筹资

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 13 日，纳斯达克上市公司 Cipher Digital（CIFR）计划通过发行 8.5 亿美元零息可转换票据筹集资金，用于支持其 Barber Lake 项目，并扩大高性能计算（HPC）数据中心业务。

该公司在 10 月 13 日的公告中表示，此次私募发行规模最高可增至 10 亿美元，前提是初始购买方行使额外购买 1.5 亿美元票据的选择权。此外，Cipher 还计划将部分现有的、票面利率为 1.75%、2030 年到期的可转换票据置换为普通股。

此次融资正值该公司调整位于得克萨斯州科罗拉多城的 Barber Lake 项目开发计划之后。相关调整延长了项目的合同期限，同时增加了 Cipher 承担的建设成本。该公司 9 月表示，与 Fluidstack 及一家未具名人工智能实验室达成的协议，将使该设施的合同租赁期限从 10 年延长至 20 年，合同收入也将从 38 亿美元增至超过 90 亿美元。

items.content:
Russia clears Sberbank for crypto trading ahead of December launch
Russia’s largest bank, Sberbank, has secured crypto exchange authorization as it prepares to offer Bitcoin, Ether and Tether USDt trading.
Sberbank, Russia’s largest lender, has secured the central bank’s approval to trade cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, ahead of a planned December launch.
The Bank of Russia’s updated register, dated Tuesday, lists 10 authorized crypto exchange operators and six digital custodians, up from four and five, respectively, a week earlier. The lists include major lenders Sberbank and VTB alongside nonbank companies such as T-Invest Lab and Atomyze.
Sberbank previously said it plans to launch crypto products supporting Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and Tether’s USDt (USDT) on Dec. 1, 2026, through its existing SberBank Online, SberInvestments and SberBusiness platforms.
Sberbank has already begun testing crypto purchases, sales, deposits and withdrawals through its SberBank Online app, Russian business newspaper Vedomosti reported on Thursday, citing the bank’s press office. The bank said the final launch timeline depends on additional central bank regulations.
The registrations follow the Sept. 1 entry into force of Russia’s new crypto rules, which placed exchange operators and custodians under central bank oversight. The country still prohibits using cryptocurrencies to pay for goods and services.
Sberbank was among the first companies to secure digital custodian status last Tuesday.
Related: UK sanctions three crypto exchanges tied to Russian illicit funds
items.title: Russia clears Sberbank for crypto trading ahead of December launch

Wintermute: Crypto Is Losing Its Flow Support as ETF Outflows Mount

Wintermute said crypto is losing support from capital flows, while equities remain backed by earnings expectations. Last week, BTC fell 3.2% and ETH dropped 7.0%, with U.S. spot BTC and ETH ETFs recording $679M and $542M in net outflows, respectively. BTC ETF outflows were the largest weekly total since late June.

Wintermute said a sustained recovery requires long-term Treasury yields to stabilize and spot ETF flows to turn positive. Until then, BTC remains vulnerable to volatility and downside risks, while low-quality altcoin rallies should be approached cautiously. The firm remains constructive long term but would turn more cautious if the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield exceeds 5.64% or BTC repeatedly fails to break above $82,500. — link

South Korea blocks 27 crypto exchanges, including Bitmart and Kucoin
The country’s regulators are stepping up their earlier restrictions on mobile apps to websites, targeting unregistered exchanges before investors report losses.
- South Korea is blocking the websites of 27 unregistered cryptocurrency exchanges, including KuCoin, BitMart and MEXC, after restricting access to their mobile apps last year.
- Foreign exchanges must register with the Financial Intelligence Unit and meet security and anti-money-laundering requirements to legally serve South Korean customers.
- Regulators warned that customers of unauthorized platforms may struggle to recover funds and urged investors to verify registration and withdraw their assets.
South Korea is blocking access to 27 unregistered crypto exchanges' websites, including KuCoin, BitMart, and MEXC, extending its crackdown on foreign trading platforms beyond just their mobile apps.
The country’s Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) announced Tuesday that the Korea Communications Standards Commission approved the restrictions following reviews on Oct. 6 and 7. Websites operated from overseas will be blocked, while those operating domestically face service termination, the FIU noted.
The move closes another route for South Korean investors to access unregistered exchanges after authorities restricted access to their mobile apps on Google and Apple last year. Regulators can now seek website blocks as soon as they detect unregistered activity, without waiting for a court ruling or evidence that customers have lost money.
The FIU did not specify how long the restrictions will last or set a deadline for the exchanges to register. However, any exchange that wants to legally operate in the country and serve South Korean customers must register with the FIU and meet the country’s security and anti-money laundering (AML) requirements.
“We respect applicable laws and regulations across jurisdictions and continuously strengthen our compliance framework in response to evolving regulatory requirements,” a KuCoin spokesperson said.
“User assets remain safe and secure, and we will communicate any further updates through our official channels.”
BitMart, Phemex and MEXC did not immediately respond to a CoinDesk request for comment.
South Korea's proposed Digital Asset Basic Law, yet to come into force, would set the groundwork for a legal framework for digital assets, including issuance, trading, custody and supervision. The country’s Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory service announced new rules in April, removing the discretion exchanges had to let users bypass holding periods.
The FIU said it has referred 44 unregistered operators to investigators and will seek further blocks against websites that reopen under different addresses. Only 28 virtual asset service providers are currently registered with the regulator.
The financial watchdog also warned that traders using unauthorized platforms could face difficulties recovering their funds. The FIU said it will work with the Digital Asset eXchange Alliance (DAXA), an industry association, to help affected customers withdraw their funds where access restrictions create problems. It also urged investors to check whether their exchange is registered and to withdraw assets from unauthorized operators.
South Korean investors have been gradually moving large amounts of crypto overseas for months due to stricter rules, with an estimated $110 billion leaving domestic exchanges in 2025.
